title: Audit streaming pipeline patterns and retention rationale
body:
Executive summary:

This note captures recommended streaming pipeline patterns for audit data, practical retention and indexing rationale, and a lightweight control-evidence workflow to tie RBAC v2 actions and control attestations into SIEM-friendly exports. Purpose is to standardize how collectors emit records, how we index and compress for search and forensic retrieval, and how to retain minimal evidence required for compliance while keeping storage and retrieval costs bounded.

Goals and constraints:
- Preserve an unambiguous chain-of-custody marker for control evidence related to RBAC changes, escalations, and policy evaluations.
- Ensure SIEM exports are predictable (schema stability) and low-latency for critical alerts.
- Design retention layers (hot/warm/cold/airgap) with clear TTLs, purge-safe markers, and legal hold overrides.
- Make collectors resilient to intermittent control-plane outages and enable backfill/repair with idempotency controls.
- Keep per-token / per-event storage cost reasonable using deduplication and sampling for non-actionable telemetry.

Scope (what's in/out):
- In scope: API audit events (authN/authZ decisions, RBAC v2 policy evaluations, role changes, token issuance/revocation), control evidence snapshots (policy text + evaluation result), evidence indexing keys, SIEM mapping and export format.
- Out of scope: application-level business logs, raw model inputs/outputs (handled by separate privacy pipeline).

High-level pipeline patterns (three canonical flows):
1) Real-time critical path (authZ-critical):
   - Producers: API gateway, auth service, RBAC v2 engine.
   - Transport: streaming broker (Kafka/Kinesis) topic with strict schema and partitions keyed by principal_id.
   - Consumers: realtime-enricher -> mini-OLAP for alerts -> SIEM-exporter.
   - Use case: immediate alerting (privilege escalation, anomalous token use).

2) Buffered evidence pipeline (forensic-ready):
   - Producers: same as above. Events are written to write-ahead log (WAL) and object store snapshots every N events.
   - Transport: tiered, with long-term storage in compressed, chunked Parquet/NDJSON blobs aligned on hour/day boundaries.
   - Consumers: backfill/replay workers and legal-hold retrievers.

3) Low-fidelity telemetry path (costed sampling):
   - Producers: sampled audit telemetry (rate-limited by producer).
   - Purpose: product telemetry and capacity planning. Not suitable for control evidence.

Schema guidance (stable contract):
- Keep one authoritative audit event schema for SIEM: fields MUST be present as strings unless explicitly specified. Required fields: event_id, timestamp_utc, principal_id, principal_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome (allow/deny/error), rbac_policy_version, evaluation_trace_ref, evidence_bucket_ref, signature_meta_ref, service_name, region.
- Use canonical UTC ISO-8601 timestamps and strictly monotonic event_id generation per producer (producer_id:event_seq).
- evaluation_trace_ref: short opaque id (10–16 chars) that links to the policy evaluation trace object in the evidence layer.
- evidence_bucket_ref: pointer to the blob containing the minimal control evidence snapshot for that evaluation (policy text, attributes, input snapshot).
- signature_meta_ref: reference to a detached signature artifact proving the record immutability (see "Chain markers" below).

Control evidence snapshot format (compact):
- Must be self-contained for a single evaluation: {policy_id, policy_version, decision_inputs (hash-only for large inputs), decision_output, timestamp, evaluator_id, evaluation_trace_id}.
- If inputs cannot be embedded due to size, include an input_blob_ref and an input_hash.

Indexing patterns and searchable keys:
- Primary index: (principal_id + timestamp) for user-centric queries.
- Secondary indexes: resource_id, action, outcome, policy_id, evaluation_trace_id.
- Tagging: add environment (prod/stage), region, and deployment_id to support scoped queries.
- Maintain a lightweight materialized view in OLAP for last-30-days hot queries; archive older data to object store with precomputed partitions (by date and principal shard).

Retention tiers and TTL rationale (recommended defaults):
- Hot (0–30 days): full fidelity, indexed, fast search. Rationale: most investigations completed within 2–3 weeks.
- Warm (31–180 days): compressed, reduced indexing (only primary + critical secondary indexes). Rationale: ongoing investigations and regulatory windows.
- Cold (181–730 days / 6–24 months depending on region): archive blobs in read-optimized format, require retrieval job. Rationale: regulators often require 1–2 year retention for access logs; we default to 2 years for critical events and 1 year for routine audits.
- Airgapped/legal-hold (indefinite until release): for litigation or active compliance investigations.

- Policy note: RBAC modification events (role grants, revocations, policy changes) get extended retention + immutable marking for at least 24 months in most jurisdictions.

Chain markers and proof artifacts (minimal proofchain):
- Each evidence blob must be accompanied by: created_at, blob_hash (SHA256), signer_id, signature (detached), and an anchoring marker stored in the WAL (small footprint).
- Anchoring approach: store a concise anchor record in a append-only ledger (topic) that records (event_id, blob_hash, signer_id, timestamp). This ledger is replicated and retained according to immutability windows.
- Purpose: allow verification that an evidence snapshot has not been altered since signing (for auditors).

Collector behavior and failure modes:
- Idempotency: collectors must attach producer_id + sequence and support de-duplication consumer-side.
- Backpressure: producers should have bounded queue and circuit-breaker behavior; on overflow, write minimal emergency record with reason and link to local WAL for later ingestion.
- Offline capture: gateways must persist critical events locally (encrypted WAL) for up to 72h if unable to reach broker; enrichers run repair jobs to reconcile.

SIEM export mapping and transformations:
- Export format: NDJSON with enforced flat fields (no nested objects). The exporter flattens evidence references to strings and attaches a small severity field (low/med/high) produced by enrichment rules.
- Field mapping: event_id -> id, timestamp_utc -> @timestamp, principal_id -> user.name, outcome -> event.outcome, action -> event.action. Keep rbac_policy_version as context field.
- Throttling: exporter has a throttling policy that ensures critical alerts always pass; noisy deny events should be collapsed with a sampling key per principal_action within a 1-minute window.

Operational playbook (short):
- Missing evidence: triage job that (1) marks incomplete events, (2) tries to rehydrate from producer WAL, (3) escalates if rehydration fails after 6h.
- Purge requests: require legal hold check and two-person approval before purge; purge jobs write an audit tombstone entry (id, who, when, reason) appended to the ledger.
- Key rotations: signature keys rotate quarterly; old signatures remain verifiable via stored public keys in key registry.

Implementation roadmap (next milestones):
- M1 (2 weeks): finalize canonical SIEM schema and add validation layer to producers.
- M2 (6 weeks): implement evaluation_trace_ref and minimal evidence snapshot emitter in RBAC v2 service.
- M3 (10 weeks): build SIEM exporter with throttling and sampling policy; smoke test with SOC.
- M4 (16 weeks): implement archival job and retrieval flow; legal-hold flow + purge approval UI.

Open questions and TODOs:
- What exact retention windows must be configurable per-customer (enterprise/private deployments)? TODO: product ask from compliance sales.
- How much of the policy text must be embedded in evidence blobs vs stored in a separate policy registry with version pointers? Tradeoff: duplication vs retrieval speed.
- Define the canonical severity enrichment rules with SOC.

Notes to reviewers (quick asks):
- Review the required audit schema fields for completeness and suggest any missing fields for our SIEM (Splunk/Elastic) mapping.
- Validate retention defaults against legal and APAC data residency constraints.
- Confirm the acceptability of detached signature anchoring in the append-only ledger model.

This is intentionally pragmatic: keep evidence snapshots small, anchor integrity proofs, give SOC immediate visibility for critical events, and push bulk storage to cost-optimized archives. If accepted, I'll turn this into a short PRD with wireframes for the purge approval UI and a small prototype exporter for testing with SOC.
